body:
In Michigan, painting the outside of a typical 2,000 sq ft home costs about **$3,060 to $8,160** in 2026, or $1.53 to $4.08 per square foot of living area. That is our estimate, built from national prices and what painters in Michigan actually earn: a median of $24.35 an hour, 3% above the national median of $23.75.

| | Michigan | National |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per sq ft of home | $1.53 to $4.08 | $1.50 to $4.00 |
| 2,000 sq ft home | $3,060 to $8,160 | $3,000 to $8,000 |
| Painter median wage | $24.35 an hour | $23.75 an hour |

## Michigan exterior painting cost by home size

| Home size (living area) | Typical cost in Michigan |
| --- | --- |
| 1,500 sq ft | $2,295 to $6,120 |
| 2,000 sq ft | $3,060 to $8,160 |
| 2,500 sq ft | $3,825 to $10,200 |
| 3,000 sq ft | $4,590 to $12,240 |

These are typical ranges for a full repaint with normal prep. A small, simple house with sound paint lands near the low end. Two stories, heavy scraping, wood repairs or premium paint push you toward the top. Enter your own home size and any quote you have in the calculator above.

## Prices in Michigan's largest metro areas

Painter wages are not the same across the state, so neither are prices. Here is the same 2,000 sq ft house in Michigan's major metro areas:

| Metro area | Painter median wage | 2,000 sq ft home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detroit-Warren-Dearborn | $27.08 | $3,337 to $8,897 |
| Ann Arbor | $28.47 | $3,477 to $9,272 |
| Lansing-East Lansing | $25.68 | $3,195 to $8,520 |
| Grand Rapids-Wyoming-Kentwood | $23.50 | $2,975 to $7,933 |

The gap between Ann Arbor and Grand Rapids-Wyoming-Kentwood is $4.97 an hour in wages, which works out to roughly $502 to $1,339 on this one job. Small towns and rural areas usually sit closer to the lower metro numbers.

## What affects the price in Michigan

**Siding.** Vinyl siding dominates new homes in the Great Lakes states. In the East North Central region, which includes Michigan, 71% of new single-family homes started in 2025 had vinyl as the main wall material, according to NAHB. Vinyl is often left unpainted, so on a newer vinyl-sided house the paint job may be mostly trim, doors and porches. Older wood-sided houses need scraping, priming and caulking first, which is where the hours go.

**Weather and timing.** Winters here are too cold for exterior paint. Sherwin-Williams says the air, the surface and the paint all need to be at or above 35°F, and the first 48 hours after painting are the critical drying window. In practice that leaves late spring to early fall, which is also when painters are busiest. Booking in late winter for a spring start often gets you a better date, and sometimes a better price.

**Prep.** On older houses, scraping peeling paint, replacing soft boards, caulking and spot-priming can take longer than the painting itself. If two quotes are far apart, compare the prep each one includes before you compare the totals. Our [national guide to exterior painting costs](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-exterior/) covers the other price factors in detail.

## Hiring a painter in Michigan

Michigan requires contractors offering residential building or maintenance and alteration work of $600 or more in labor and materials to be licensed by the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA). LARA does not list painting among its alteration trades on its homeowner page, so if you are unsure whether your job is covered, search the LARA license database or call its Residential Builders section. Either way, ask for a certificate of liability insurance.

If your house was built before 1978, the old paint may contain lead. Under EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, contractors who disturb that paint must be certified lead-safe and follow containment and cleanup steps. Ask to see the firm's certification before work starts, and expect it to add some cost.

Get at least two or three written quotes that list the same things: which surfaces, how many coats, which paint line, what prep and repairs, and who cleans up. A quote far below the range usually skips prep or uses fewer coats.

## How we worked out these prices

National data from Angi, reported by NerdWallet, puts exterior painting at $1.50 to $4 per square foot of living area. Angi says labor makes up 75% to 95% of a professional paint job. We took 80% as the labor share and adjusted that part by Michigan's painter wage compared with the national median, using Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data:

**Michigan rate = national rate × (0.2 + 0.8 × $24.35 ÷ $23.75) = national rate × 1.020**

Paint and supplies cost about the same everywhere, so only the labor part moves. Treat the results as a planning range, not a quote. Local demand, the season and each painter's overhead all shift real prices.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house in Michigan?

About $3,060 to $8,160 for the outside, with most jobs in the middle of that range. In Ann Arbor expect more, about $3,477 to $9,272.

### Where in Michigan is exterior painting most expensive?

Of the metro areas above, Ann Arbor has the highest painter wages at $28.47 an hour, and Grand Rapids-Wyoming-Kentwood the lowest at $23.50. Prices follow wages because labor is most of the bill.

### When is the best time to paint a house in Michigan?

Late spring to early fall, when the air and walls stay at or above 35°F and you can count on two dry days in a row. Book early: painters fill their calendars by spring.

### Do I need a licensed painter in Michigan?

Michigan requires contractors offering residential building or maintenance and alteration work of $600 or more in labor and materials to be licensed by the Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs (LARA). LARA does not list painting among its alteration trades on its homeowner page, so if you are unsure whether your job is covered, search the LARA license database or call its Residential Builders section.
